findings.summary: The noise estimate rests on only one or two window-to-window differences, so it is a coarse bar.
findings.evidence: The noise is the maximum of |w1-w2| and |w2-w3|. With 80 landings, one unusual older window sets the bar for every review. The design doc names the steady-trend blind spot, and the one-job floors limit false positives, so it is acceptable for now. A spread over more windows, or a rolling median absolute deviation, would be steadier once history allows.

findings.summary: The median noise windows count only measured landings, while the waste windows count all landings, so their cuts can differ slightly.
findings.evidence: median_windows slices landed_jobs(), which leaves out landed jobs that ran no model. waste_windows uses ranked_landings(), which includes them. The effect is small, and only when a landed job ran no model.

findings.summary: A retry only counts against the first-attempt share when its request text says 'try again on <job>'.
findings.evidence: It uses reading::retried_job, Athena's own retry reference, which is data-based rather than a guess. A request filed again without that reference counts as a first attempt.

summary: The change does what the request asks, but I could not run the core behavior tests myself. My local `cargo test -p athena-core` runs failed to compile: the build cache holds an out-of-date copy of a dependency built from the old code. The override that would force a rebuild was denied, so I stopped. The pass for criteria 1-5 therefore rests on the recorded CI `cargo test --locked` run for this commit plus my reading of each test. What I did run myself: the record round-trip tests (`cargo test -p athena-data throughput_review`, all 3 pass) and the grep for the old doc wording (no matches). What the change does: `athena status` and the throughput review now show three measures of wasted work over the newest 20 landings and the 20 before them: attempts per landed change, money spent on attempts that did not land, and the share of changes that landed on the first attempt. A rise of more than 20% in any of them triggers a review (new `wasted` trigger) even with the median unchanged. An open earlier design request no longer stops the review; the note and THROUGHPUT.md name it. A design request, and with 60+ landings a slowdown request, is queued only when a measure worsened beyond both the noise between older windows and a one-job floor, and the note says which. The tests assert the requested values: 2.0 attempts per landing, 0.5 first-attempt share, a spend-triggered review with a flat median, the no-skip case, and within-noise vs beyond-noise. The record gains an optional `waste` field, so old records still parse. The CHANGELOG and docs match the code, and all six changed files are on the deliverables list. The real repository has 388 landings, so the 60-landing need for a noise estimate does not hold back reviews there. Remaining findings are minor: a coarse noise estimate from one or two window differences, and small inconsistencies in how windows are cut and retries detected.
